data.title: Two chairs at the opinion table
data.goal: Two chairs at the opinion table

memoryNodes.cue: Jo asks what supports a claim.

data.situation:
By the far wall, two chairs faced a small table. Nora had invited a regular visitor and a volunteer to discuss the timetable. Each brought a different perspective. The visitor put forward a proposition to move every class online; the volunteer’s contention was that some activities depended on meeting in person. Jo wrote down the visitor’s assertion that no one would mind the change, then asked what evidence supported it. The sensitivity of the discussion became clear when the visitor mentioned people who could not use a computer. Objectivity meant recording the different accounts accurately, not pretending they were identical. Nora wanted the public discourse around the repairs to include these practical concerns. Neither guest had to win the conversation for the article to become more useful. Visitor: My proposition is to move all the classes online.
Volunteer: From my perspective, that would exclude some people.
Jo: Could we check how many people need an in-person option?

The sensitivity of the discussion became clear when the visitor mentioned people who could not use a computer. readingBlocks.zh: 靠远墙的两把椅子面对一张小桌。诺拉请一位常来的访客和一名志愿者讨论时间表，两人带来不同视角。访客提出把所有课程都搬到网上的建议，志愿者则认为有些活动需要当面参与。乔记下访客“没人会介意变化”的断言，再问有什么证据。谈到无法使用电脑的人时，大家意识到讨论需要谨慎。客观意味着准确记录不同说法，而不是假装它们一致。诺拉希望围绕维修的公共讨论能包括这些实际问题。文章变得有用，并不要求谁在交谈中获胜。

glossary.zh: 观察或考虑问题的观点；视角
glossary.note: from someone’s perspective；a perspective on something。
glossary.example: The volunteer offered a different perspective.
glossary.exampleZh: 志愿者提供了不同视角。

externalEvidence.definition: a way of regarding situations or topics etc.

glossary.zh: 提出供考虑的计划或建议
glossary.note: put forward a proposition：提出一项建议；这里讨论把课程搬到网上的计划。
glossary.example: The visitor’s proposition was to move classes online.
glossary.exampleZh: 访客提出把课程搬到网上。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.publisher: Oxford University Press / Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: sense 1 suggestion/plan; sense 4 formal statement of opinion

glossary.note: 可数名词；某人肯定地声称某事是真的，需要检查支持依据。它既可能真也可能假，不等于已证实事实。
glossary.example: Jo questioned the assertion that no one would mind.
glossary.exampleZh: 乔质疑了没人会介意的断言。

glossary.note: someone’s contention that…；这里不是争执这个义。
glossary.example: The volunteer’s contention was that some classes needed a room.
glossary.exampleZh: 志愿者的论点是有些课程需要场地。

externalEvidence.definition: a point asserted as part of an argument

glossary.zh: 不因个人偏见而歪曲事实的客观性
glossary.note: maintain objectivity；客观不要求把不同说法写成同一个说法。

externalEvidence.definition: judgment based on observable phenomena and uninfluenced by emotions or personal prejudices

glossary.zh: 话题或信息因可能触动、冒犯他人而需要谨慎处理的敏感性质
glossary.note: the sensitivity of an issue；与仪器灵敏度区分。
glossary.example: Jo recognised the sensitivity of the discussion.
glossary.exampleZh: 乔意识到讨论的敏感性质。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.publisher: Oxford University Press / Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary

glossary.zh: 围绕某个问题展开的谈论或论述
glossary.note: public discourse；较正式，指一系列讨论而非一次闲聊。
glossary.example: The article contributed to public discourse about the repairs.
glossary.exampleZh: 文章参与了关于维修的公共讨论。

externalEvidence.definition: an extended communication (often interactive) dealing with some particular topic
